turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Doctor: Hello, I’m your doctor today. What brings you in today? Patient: I’m here for my annual well-check, but I’ve also noticed a rough, scaly, sandpaper-like patch on the left back of my hand. It doesn’t hurt and there’s no tenderness.
How long have you had this rough, scaly patch on the back of your hand?
I think it’s been there for a few months now, and it hasn’t been getting painful or very tender.
Has the size or appearance of the patch changed over the time you've noticed it?
I’d say it hasn’t changed much in size, but the rough, scaly quality seems about the same as when I first noticed it. It looks fairly consistent on the left back of my hand.
Have you noticed any other similar patches on other parts of your body?
Patient: No, I haven’t noticed any similar patches anywhere else on my body. It seems to be only on the left back of my hand.
Have you had a lot of sun exposure to your hands, or do you work outdoors?

“Yes, I do spend time outdoors quite often, and I’ve been walking and sunbathing for years, including on sunny days where my hands are exposed. I don’t work outdoors professionally, but my hands do get regular sun.”
Have you used any protective measures like sunscreen or clothing to cover your hands when you're outdoors?
I usually don’t use sunscreen specifically on my hands, and I tend to wear short sleeves so they’re often exposed to the sun. I haven’t been covering that area much when I’m outside.

Given the history of chronic sun exposure and the description of the lesion, I'm starting to lean towards a few specific diagnoses. However, I need a bit more information to be more confident. 

How would you describe the border of the patch - is it well-defined or does it blend in with the surrounding skin?

Patient: The border feels pretty well-defined, like the patch has a clear edge against the surrounding skin, and the rough, scaly texture stays pretty consistent within that area. It doesn’t seem to blend into the rest of the hand.
[DDX] Actinic keratosis, Squamous cell carcinoma, Bowen's disease, Seborrheic keratosis, Keratoacanthoma
